goal: A claim-store liveness sweep batch-releases every claim whose lease has lapsed at an injected now -- returning those tasks to the acquirable pool and dropping them from list_claims -- including all of one dead worker's claims in a single pass, while leaving still-valid claims held.

relevant: .flywheel/specs/00049-distributed-scheduling-metadata.md -- acceptance criteria #11, #12, #13 (sweep part), #17 and decision D-6 this task satisfies

packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_claims.py -- the ClaimStore protocol and SqliteClaimStore: add the sweep operation reading lease_expires_at against an injected now; note list_claims today does not filter expiry
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_claims_postgres.py -- mirror the same sweep on the Postgres backend
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_orchestrator_claims.py -- keep this suite green; it pins acquire/renew/release/list and injects now for deterministic lease expiry
constraints: The sweep takes an injected now and releases every claim whose lease_expires_at <= now: those task ids become acquirable by any worker and are no longer reported as live-held by list_claims. A claim whose lease is still valid at now stays held, owned by its worker, and not acquirable by another worker.
A single sweep releases ALL lapsed claims belonging to the same worker in one pass -- per-worker dead-worker reaping, not one task at a time.
now MUST be injected (do not read a wall clock) so lease expiry stays deterministic and testable, matching the existing claim store.
The behavior holds on BOTH the SQLite and Postgres claim-store backends.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do NOT add a heartbeat_at column -- lease_expires_at already encodes liveness; heartbeat is the existing lease renewal (D-6).
Do NOT write a persistent reclaim/heartbeat event ledger -- that is spec 00051 (D-6); the sweep's effect is graded on claim-store end-state only.
Do NOT change acquire/renew/release semantics for non-lapsed claims (#17).
Do NOT modify flywheel-core; do NOT modify files under tests/ or weaken existing claim assertions.
edge_cases: Two claims with different lease windows, now advanced past only one: after the sweep the lapsed task is absent from list_claims and freshly acquirable, while the still-valid claim remains listed, owned, and not acquirable by another worker.
One worker holding three lapsed claims: a single sweep frees all three (not one-at-a-time).
A sweep with no lapsed claims is a no-op leaving every claim held and owned.
